english.note: Use this as the everyday noun phrase for a large, usually tangible quantity; it is the all-purpose choice among the quantity renderings here.
Use this as the all-purpose choice for a large amount or a lot of things.
Use this for a large amount or number, especially in phrases such as 一大堆禮物.
Use this before a noun such as 工作 when “a ton of” means a very large amount rather than a literal weight.
Use this as the all-purpose colloquial choice for a large amount or loose pile, such as a bunch of trouble.
Use this for a large amount of something, especially when the amount is emphasized rather than the neat arrangement.
Use this for a huge heap or quantity, rather than for a literal landform.
Use this for a large pile or quantity of items in expressions such as a host of parts.
Use this for a large quantity or number, usually before or instead of naming the things involved.
Use this for a figurative forest-like mass or large amount, such as a large amount of criticism.
